author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read the GitHub Enterprise Cloud audit log. GitHub writes it to an Amazon S3 bucket through log streaming, as gzip files of JSON lines, and a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest (customer-managed) integration reads the bucket. Sign-ins, failed sign-ins, sign-outs and 2FA challenges go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- Stream the enterprise audit log to an Amazon S3 bucket (Enterprise settings > Audit log > Log streaming) and read the bucket with a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest (customer-managed) integration.
- GitHub writes gzip files of JSON lines, one event per line; Sophos doesn't document whether its forwarding function reads gzip files, so check that the first events arrive.
- Source IP addresses appear only after Enable source IP disclosure is turned on.

Field mapping:
- Sign-ins, failed sign-ins, sign-outs and 2FA challenges go to Auth (GitHub logs these only for Enterprise Managed Users).
- Every other event (git, repository, organization, enterprise, token and policy changes) goes to CloudAudit with the action as the event name.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the fields in GitHub's audit log docs with made-up values.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (121 of 121 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same events there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these events in 11 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- The Azure Event Hubs stream's message format isn't documented, so it isn't covered.
